transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ben Carter, Samira Khan, Lina Ortiz (Redwood) - Maya Patel, Greg Santos, Nina Zhou, Laura Kim, Tom Rios (Skyline Apps)

Summary:
Skyline is mid-poc focusing on embedding Redwood via our SDK for in-app assistant features and using tool/function calls to hit structured output targets for invoices and entitlement flows. This week covered results from first week of integration, SDK edge-cases, KV cache behavior, and next-step items: more targeted benchmarks, sandbox keys, and a VPC/KMS deep-dive.

Topics:
- SDK integration issues (timeouts, retries)
- Tool/function calling semantics and retries
- Structured output extraction (JSON vs custom tokens)
- Performance: latency and batching tradeoffs
- Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Ben: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check 
d


is this still the time that works for you?
[00:07] Maya: yeah this is good, thanks Ben. we have Greg and Nina dialed in, Laura's on for the product questions and Tom for infra.
[00:13] Ben: perfect. quick agenda: review the week one integration results, any SDK bugs, structured-output accuracy, and then next steps. Samira will walk through the SDK snippets.
[00:25] Samira: great; so i uploaded the sandbox keys yesterday, you should have access to the redwood sandbox - link in the email, but i'll paste the sheet after. first thing we saw 
d


couple of 502s when using the function/tool call pattern with streaming enabled, likely around our end-of-stream handling.
[00:40] Greg: mhm we saw that too, especially when we do concurrent calls from the mobile clients. appears to correlate with their reconnect logic.
[00:50] Samira: okay makes sense. one immediate mitigation is to enable short client-side retries with idempotency keys; the SDK has a retry helper. i'll attach the snippet: sample_retries.js in the shared drive.
[01:05] Nina: small note 
d

the structured output schema we provided has nested objects and the model sometimes emits arrays as strings, like "[object Object]" or extra commas. any tips on getting more consistent JSON?
[01:18] Samira: yeah, structured output is sensitive. two levers: 1) use the SDK's structured_output mode which includes a schema enforcement pass and 2) use function signatures for hard typing. we noticed with larger context and the K V cache, sometimes the prefix tokens change the output. also, we sometimes seen 'K V cash' in transcriptions 

 d


 i mean the KV cache 

 d


 sorry.
[01:40] Ben: (laughs) classic transcription.
[01:45] Laura: can you explain the function-calling pattern again? are we supposed to call the tool from the client or from a backend worker?
[01:54] Samira: best practice is server-side for secret management. let the model return a function call payload, then your backend executes the tool. for mobile, the client can call the backend proxy which then calls Redwood. avoids embedding keys on device.
[02:10] Tom: from an infra standpoint, we're evaluating Redwood Dedicated vs hosted. Dedicated is attractive for predictable throughput, but we have strict egress rules and want VPC peering + customer KMS. what's required?
[02:22] Ben: Dedicated supports VPC connectors + customer-managed KMS; we can provide the network guide. for the POC, hosted with a VPC egress IP allowlist is fastest, but if you need no egress to public internet, Dedicated or Private is the route. we'll send a doc.
[02:40] Maya: our security team asked about audit logs and retention, SOC2/ISO. do you provide per-request audit logs and integrations with our SIEM?
[02:49] Lina: yes we have audit logs shipped to S3 or your SIEM, retention configurable by plan. we'll include the SOC2 pack and our compliance matrix.
[02:58] Greg: back to performance 

 d


 we ran a small benchmark using the mini-runner. average token latency was ~85ms with batching off, and 40ms when we used continuous batching with a batch size of 8 on the sandbox. does that sync with your expectations?
[03:15] Samira: that sounds reasonable for the hosted hardware profile you're on. if you pin to Dedicated GPU pools you'll see more predictable p90s. also quantization profiles matter for cost.
[03:27] Nina: we tried model redwood/gptx-large-8q and got some hallucinations in invoice extraction; should we change models or adjust prompts?
[03:36] Samira: for structured output with high precision, try our specialized extraction model variant 

 d

 d redwood-extract-v1 (note: internal name in convo may be different). also try function schema enforcement; often it's a prompt + schema combo.
[03:50] Laura: is function calling stable across streaming? we need to stream partial content while also returning a structured JSON at the end.
[03:58] Samira: yes, but you need to buffer until the function call completed. streaming tokens are emitted, but the function call object arrives as a separate event. the SDK has a streaming handler to assemble that; i'll include the example. small caveat: some SDKs may surface the event differently, we had mobile websockets differences.
[04:18] Ben: can we walk through the failing example Nina mentioned? Nina, did you upload the failing prompts?
[04:25] Nina: yes uploaded to the sheet: row 12-19 have the invoice ID mismatches. for example the line-item amounts are sometimes concatenated into a single string 

 d


 looks like tokenization boundary issues.
[04:36] Samira: interesting. tokenization sometimes splits currency symbols. a quick hack is to include a preprompt enforcing numeric format, e.g., "Output amounts as numbers only, use cents as integer". i'll add that to the sample prompt.
[04:50] Greg: also saw error spike when multiple users hit the same session id; maybe our session sharding is off and KV cache entries conflict.
[04:59] Samira: yes session isolation is key 

 d


 ensure unique conversation ids per end-user, and set cache TTL appropriately. by default TTL is 24h but you can set shorter.
[05:10] Tom: for VPC specifics, are you supporting aws vpc endpoints or do we need to poke holes in our NAT gateway?
[05:18] Ben: we support both; for Dedicated we can peer into your VPC, for hosted you can use NAT egress with IP allowlist. we'll attach network diagrams.
[05:28] Maya: cost question 

 d


 if we do heavy batching and caching, does that materially reduce token costs? our CFO wants ballpark savings for a quarter.
[05:36] Ben: batching reduces per-request overhead and caching reduces tokens for repeated prefixes. we can model it 

 d

Samira, can you summarize the cost levers?
[05:44] Samira: sure 

 d

1) prefix/KV caching reduces tokens by up to 60% for assisted flows, 2) batching increases throughput and reduces compute per token, 3) quantized runtimes for Dedicated reduce GPU costs by ~20-40% depending on model. we'll produce a short spreadsheet with assumptions.
[06:00] Laura: for structured output, do you recommend using function signatures or schema enforcement?
[06:05] Samira: both. function signatures are deterministic for typed fields; schema enforcement helps with nested validations. start with function calls for critical fields and schema pass for post-validate.
[06:16] Nina: question about retries 

 d


 when we retry a tool call, how do we keep idempotency, especially if the tool triggers side effects?
[06:25] Samira: put idempotency keys on your tool calls from the backend; the SDK exposes the idempotency helper. if the tool is side-effectful, use two-phase commit patterns or queue actions until you confirm the call result.
[06:36] Greg: we've been using the Node SDK but ran into a type mismatch when we used the python snippets from the docs. are examples synchronized?
[06:44] Ben: docs sync is ongoing; Samira maintains a canonical examples repo. i'll link it in the notes. sometimes copy-paste leads to different param names across languages.
[06:55] Samira: i'll also paste the exact Node snippet we tested. small gotcha: the streaming handler uses event names 'token' and 'function_call' and some older SDK builds used 'tool_call' 

 d

 depends on SDK version.
[07:10] Laura: any blockers on our side preventing progress this week?
[07:15] Maya: blocked slightly on keys for the DEDICATED trial and firewall approvals. Tom is pinging infra.
[07:21] Tom: yeah i need the network diagram and ip ranges to request the firewall rule.
[07:26] Ben: we'll send that today.

 i'll share my screen and show the SDK flow (note: meeting recording shows partial screen).

 d

[08:02] Nina: thanks 

 d

 small nit, the sample uses synchronous execution; we prefer async worker queue in prod. any issues with queuing?
[08:10] Samira: none; the SDK supports async calls and you can store function_call payloads in a queue worker. just keep idempotency keys intact.
[08:21] Greg: regarding the hallucinations on redwood/gptx-large-8q, would using a smaller but extract-optimized model be better?
[08:30] Samira: yes, the extract-optimized often yields higher precision for constrained outputs at slightly higher latency; it's a tradeoff. for invoices I usually recommend extract-v1, test with small prompt set.
